lesson.title: Western tableware and consideration for food cultures
lesson.reading: ようしょくのどうぐとしょくぶんかへのはいりょ

objectives.text: Read basic Western placement and in-progress/finished signals
Ask about cultural differences without assumptions
Connect halal and vegetarian terminology to confirmation

sections.title: Course progression and equipment placement
sections.body: The manual’s Western course example progresses through hors d’oeuvre, soup, fish, meat, dessert and coffee. Menus vary, but the sequence helps plan preparations from beginning to end. Around the plate, use forks on the left, knives and spoons on the right, dessert utensils above and the bread plate at the upper left as basic positions. When there are many utensils, check their use order and placement rather than symmetry alone. Replenish missing equipment before the dish arrives so there is no last-minute rush.

sections.title: Use order and dining signals
sections.body: The basic approach described is a knife in the right hand and a fork in the left. Use multiple utensils from the outside inward. A separated, inverted-V arrangement on the plate indicates eating is in progress, while parallel utensils toward the lower right suggest the meal is finished. Do not decide every guest’s intention from placement alone. Politely asking before clearing avoids taking a plate the guest still wants. Use manners as clues for smooth service, not to judge guests. A butter spreader is the special utensil used to spread butter on bread. Distinguish its role from dining knives and check which utensils to provide.

sections.title: Confirm what the guest can eat
sections.body: Food habits differ by country, culture and personal outlook. Halal concerns what is permitted under Islamic teachings and requires checking food and preparation methods. Pork-derived ingredients and alcohol matter, but their absence alone does not prove every dish is halal-suitable. Vegetarian also does not mean everyone eats exactly the same foods. Rather than deciding from the label, ask which ingredients the guest avoids and what conditions need checking, then provide information confirmed with the kitchen.

sections.title: Explain what you do not yet know
sections.body: Recommending an unverified dish as “probably fine” can damage trust. Separate confirmed facts from what remains unknown. Say, “May I check the ingredients with the kitchen? Thank you for waiting,” then report the result. Explain honestly if some conditions cannot be accommodated. Do not pressure the guest to eat the same meal as others; provide accurate information for their choice. If you cannot answer alone, involve the manager or knowledgeable staff.

terms.meaning: Knives, forks and spoons used for eating
An appetizer served at the beginning of a Western course
A term for what is permitted in Islamic teachings
A name for plant-centered food habits; confirm the person’s specific conditions
A utensil for spreading butter or similar foods on bread.

example.situation: A guest says they do not eat meat. A staff member assumes a soup is suitable because no meat is visible.
steps: Ask which foods and conditions need checking.
Confirm the soup’s actual ingredients with the kitchen.
Explain verified information and the facility’s limits so the guest can choose.

practice.prompt: Draw a Western place setting and explain utensil order and meal signals. Then describe what to check when asked “Is this halal?” or told “I avoid meat.”
expectedPoints: Explain the layout from the guest’s viewpoint
Use signals as clues and confirm completion
Do not decide ingredients or suitability from a cultural label alone

questions.prompt: What is the basic order for multiple utensils?
choices: Inside first
Outside first
Most expensive first
Largest first
questions.explanation: The basic order is outside inward, not by size or price.

questions.prompt: Two utensils are aligned toward the lower right. What is appropriate?
choices: Treat it as a possible finish signal and ask before clearing
Assume eating must still be in progress and never respond
Scold the guest and reposition them
Ignore intention and clear every plate immediately
questions.explanation: The arrangement suggests completion, but confirm the guest’s intention before clearing.

questions.prompt: How should you recommend a dish with no visible meat to a vegetarian guest?
choices: Guarantee it from appearance alone
Ask them to eat the same food as everyone else
Assume all people using the label have identical conditions
Confirm their conditions and the actual ingredients
questions.explanation: Appearance may not reveal ingredients. Confirm both the person’s needs and the kitchen’s information.

questions.prompt: You have confirmed only that pork and alcohol are not used. What should you say?
choices: Claim every certification is present
Guarantee suitability for every possible condition
Explain the confirmed ingredient information and check unverified conditions
Label it halal-certified without checking
questions.explanation: Do not guarantee certifications or preparation conditions that have not been confirmed.

questions.prompt: When should a butter spreader be used?
choices: To measure a wine’s region of origin
To unlock a guestroom
To calculate the bill
To spread butter on bread
questions.explanation: Prepare dining utensils according to their functions.

questions.prompt: What is the basic Western place setting from the guest’s viewpoint?
choices: Forks left, knives and spoons right, dessert utensils above, bread plate upper left
Forks always upper right and bread plate on the floor
Positions are decided only by price
The guest’s orientation does not matter
questions.explanation: Check use order and positions from the diner’s viewpoint.

questions.prompt: Which is the Western course example in the teaching material?
choices: Serve only coffee six times
Hors d’oeuvre → soup → fish → meat → dessert → coffee
Fish and meat are indistinguishable and need no utensil preparation
Replace the actual menu with the teaching example without permission
questions.explanation: The example supports preparation. Check the facility’s menu for the actual progression.

questions.prompt: What basic knife and fork grip does the teaching material describe?
choices: Hold the more expensive utensil in the right hand
Knife in the right hand, fork in the left
Knowing the use order makes grip irrelevant
Always hold everything in one hand
questions.explanation: Distinguish utensil positions, use order and grip.

questions.prompt: What basic meaning of halal does the source introduce?
choices: It only means avoiding all animal foods
It means the highest-priced dish
It means produced in a Japanese region
It concerns what Islamic teachings permit and requires checking ingredients, methods and other conditions
questions.explanation: Distinguish halal from veganism, price and origin. Knowing the name does not guarantee a whole dish’s suitability.

questions.prompt: Which interpretation of the teaching material’s utensil arrangements is appropriate?
choices: A separated inverted V means finished, and parallel lower-right utensils mean eating
Placement always proves the guest’s intention
Clear silently with either arrangement
A separated inverted V suggests eating; parallel lower-right utensils suggest finishing, and you also ask before clearing
questions.explanation: Compare the two source arrangements. Treat them as clues and confirm with the guest, rather than absolute proof of intention.

illustration.caption: Distinguish equipment placement and utensil arrangements during and after eating.
illustration.alt: A place setting with fork left, knife and spoon right, bread plate upper left and dessert utensils above
